FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 24 May 1989, after the 
draft finalized by the Forestry and Plantation Machinery Sectional Committee had been approved 
by the Agricultural and Food Products Division Council. 

Marking hammers are hand tools used by the foresters for marking on green trees in the forest. 
For marking, the bark is removed from a portion of the tree and then the marking hammer is 
struck with an impact action which creates impression on the trees for identification. 

This standard has been prepared based on the manufacturing practices prevailing in the country. 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, 
the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded 
off in accordance with IS 2: 1960 *Rules for rounding off numerical values { revised )\ The 
number of significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the 
specified value in this standard- 



IS 12703 : 1989 



Indian Standard 



FORESTRY TOOLS — TREE MARKING 
HAMMERS — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard specifies the material, dimen- 
sions and other requirements for marking 
hammers used by foresters for marking on green 
trees in the forest. 

2 REFERENCES 

The following Indian Standards are necessary 
adjuncts to this standard: 

IS No, Title 

2102 ( Part 1 ) : 1980 General tolerances for 
dimensions and form and 
position : Part 1 Gene- 
ral tolerances for linear 
and angular dimensions 
( second revision ) 

IS 2500 ( Part 1 ) : 1983 Sampling inspection 

tables : Part 1 Inspection 
by attributes and count 
of defects ( first revision ) 

3 MATERIALS 
3 A Hammers 

Shall be manufactured from mild steel. 

3.2 Handle 

Seasoned hard wood shall be used. 

4 HARDNESS 

4.1 The bottom portion of the hammer up to a 
height of 5 to 8 mm shall be hardened by chemi- 
cal heat treatment ( cyaniding ) so that the 
engraved letters attain a hardness of 40 ± 2 
HRC. 

5 SHAPE AND DIMENSIONS 

5.1 Unless otherwise agreed to between the 
purchaser and the supplier, the shape and 
dimensions of the marking hammer shall be as 
given in Fig. 1. 

5.2 The tolerances for various dimensions shall 
be of very coarse class as specified in IS 2102 
( Part 1 ) : 1980. 

6 OTHER REQUIREMENTS 

6.1 The characters of the marking hammers shall 
be machine engraved with double taper. 

6.2 The depth of engraving shall be not less 
than 5 mm. 



(**3 The apex angle of the character shall be 60 
degrees up to a height of 2 mm and afterwards, 
a suitable taper shall be provided up to the base. 



vary depending 
the text to be 



6.4 The size of the letters shall 
upon the size of hammer and 
engraved. 

6.5 The body of the marking hammer shall 
manufactured by forging. 



be 



6.6 The wooden handle 
fitted inside the eye and 
wedges. 

7 TESTS 



shall 
shall 



be 
be 



completely 
secured by 



7.1 The marking hammers shall be tested by 
striking the hammer on a sample of hard wood 
for at least 100 times. During and after the 
completion of test, the character shall not show 
any deformation. The impression created during 
the test shall be clear and easily readable. 

8 WORKMANSHIP AND FINISH 

8.1 The forging shall be free from cracks, seams, 
pits, burrs and other visual defects. 

8.2 The handle shall be smooth and shall have a 
suitable grip. 

8.3 The metallic portion shall be painted. 

8.4 The wooden handle shall be pohshed or 
lacquered. 

9 MARKING AND PACKING 

9.1 Marking 

Each marking hammer shall be marked with the 
following particulars. 

a) Manufacturers' name or recognized trade 
mark, if any; and 

b) Batch or code number. 

9.2 Packing 

The hammers shall be packed as agreed to bet- 
ween the purchaser and the supplier for safe 
handling in transit and storage. 

10 SAMPLING 

10,1 In order to ascertain the conformity of the 
lotj the procedure for sampling inspection as 
given in IS 2500 (Part I ) : 1983 shall be 
followed. The inspection level and AQL for 
various eharacteristics shall be according to tO.2 
and 10.3.

10.2 For dimensions, workmanship and finish, 
a single samphng plan with inspection level IV 
and AQL of 4 percent given in Table 1 and 2 of 
IS 2500 ( Part I ): 1983 shall be followed. 



10.3 For hardness and other requirements, a 
single sampling plan with inspection level 11 and 
AQL of 4 percent as given in Table 1 and 2 of 
IS 2500 ( Part I ); 1983 shall be followed. 



Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act^ 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quality control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to 
that standard as a further safeguard* Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards.
